newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's ONGC fiscal half year crude output falls.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC fiscal half year crude output falls.

text.p: India's state Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd's total crude oil production for the first half of the fiscal year (April 1996/March 1997) has fallen by more than 11 percent year-on-year, an ONGC spokesman said on Friday.
Monthly crude production has been falling steadily this year. Year-on-year comparisons have been lower too.
ONGC's six-month crude output stood at 14.211 million tonnes, down from 15.935 million tonnes last year.
In the latest data, September's crude oil production fell to 2.302 million tonnes, compared to 2.612 million tonnes last September.

He said crude production from the country's largest hydrocarbon producing area, the Bombay High Basin, also fell to 1.628 million tonnes in September this year, down from 1.851 million tonnes last year.

Falling production at Bombay High field has seen ONGC lower its total crude production target for this fiscal year to around 29.4 million tonnes from its actual production of 31.9 million tonnes in the last fiscal year (1995/1996), he said.
ONGC's total gas production for the fiscal year is however due to increase as production from the Basin rises, he said.

In September, gas production from the Basin rose year-on-year to 1.1259 trillion cubic metres from 1.0978 trillion cubic metres, while output from the rest of the country was stable at 320 million cubic metres. ONGC CRUDE PRODUCTION (thousand tonnes)
